purpose: Diagnostic comparison of naive stratified random-pixel holdout against the accepted V4.2 spatial evaluation; it is not a replacement primary evaluation.
scientific_question: Does random pixel holdout produce materially more optimistic apparent performance than spatially blocked extrapolation when sample counts, class counts, labels, models, and training settings are held fixed?

split_construction.eligible_universe: exact union of accepted train, validation, and test masks in the corresponding source spatial fold
split_construction.stratification: independent deterministic permutation within y=0 and y=1
split_construction.allocation: exactly match the source fold train, validation, and test counts separately for each class
split_construction.normalization: channel mean and population standard deviation fitted only on the randomized training mask

training.sampler: patch centers sampled at the natural positive prevalence among randomized training pixels that can be centers of a complete 128 by 128 grid-contained patch
training.loss: BCEWithLogitsLoss with randomized-training negative/positive pixel ratio
training.determinism: same deterministic settings as V3; no AMP and no TF32

inference.coverage: full grid by grid-contained overlapping windows

evaluation.test_label_access: once after best checkpoint is fixed
secondary_metrics: precision and recall at top 1 percent
precision and recall at top 5 percent
F1 precision and recall at fixed 0.5
evaluation.seed_ensemble: arithmetic mean of four probability maps within each model and split
evaluation.comparison: pair each Rk result with the accepted spatial fold Fk; report paired differences without treating four pairs as independent geographic replicates

diagnostic_bias_boundary.known_risk: randomly interleaved pixels share local spatial context; validation and test feature pixels can occur inside training input patches although their labels are excluded from the loss
diagnostic_bias_boundary.interpretation: higher random-holdout performance estimates optimism under a leakage-prone evaluation design, not improved geographic transfer
prohibited_claims: random holdout is a valid spatial generalization estimate

change_control.test_driven_changes: require a new protocol and complete rerun
